newsitem.title: USA: National Power eyes investments in U.S. power.
newsitem.headline: National Power eyes investments in U.S. power.

text.p: National Power Plc is eyeing acquisitions of U.S. electric power plants and greenfield construction of natural gas-fired generation as deregulation proceeds in the U.S. market, Chief Executive Keith Henry said on Tuesday.

"We'd be interested in buying the generating assets in New England," Henry said of power plants recently put on the block as part of a disaggregation of the country's monopoly electric utility industry.

Despite excess generating capacity in the U.S. domestic power market, Henry said the British power company also will consider building gas-fired plants that would be less expensive to operate and more competitive than existing coal and nuclear plants.

National Power currently has a stake in six U.S. power plants with 1,543 megawatts of capacity through its investment with independent power provider American National Power, and directly owns 680 megawatts of that capacity, he said.

The company could add about 1,000 megawatts of capacity to its U.S. holdings in the next three or four years, Henry told reporters after a speech to the Cambridge Energy Research Associates energy forum in Houston.
